examples: As you get older, time seems to pass more quickly.
As the temperature drops, the autumn leaves turn more and more red.
As urbanization advances, green spaces are decreasing.
As I gained experience, I gradually became more confident.
As time passed, the pain eased.
As it gets warmer, the number of people visiting the park is increasing
fields.explain:
Used for continuous tendencies/developments, usually natural, social or psychological phenomena.
The second clause is the resulting consequence and does not carry a direct command/volition.
Often appears in explanations, reports and data analysis.

- “The more … the more …/Along with … …”: Two phenomena change in the same direction, where a change in A brings about a corresponding change in B.
- Emphasizes a relationship of covariation/gradual change; not used for instantaneous events, and not used with volition/command in the second clause.
fields.notes:
• Besides changes in the same direction, it can also indicate changes in opposite directions (A increases, B decreases), as long as one follows the other.
• Clause A usually represents the “time basis/point of change”, and clause B is the observed result.
• Often used with words such as: 進む, 高まる, 低下する, 増える, 減る, 深まる,…
meaning_vi: The more … the more …
explain: Expresses two changes taking place in parallel: as A gradually changes, B changes along with it. Continuous and objective in character.
examples: 1. 試験が近づくにつれて、だんだん心配になってきた。
As the exam approached, I gradually became more worried.
2. 日本での生活が長くなるにつれ、友だちもできて楽しくなった。
The longer I lived in Japan, the more friends I made and the more I enjoyed it.
3. 再開発が進むにつれて、駅前の様子がすっかり変わってしまった。
As the redevelopment progressed, the area in front of the station changed completely.
4. 時間の経過につれ、その事件のことは忘れられてしまった。
As time went by, the incident was forgotten.
mistakes: Using it with an instantaneous event (×到着するにつれて驚いた) → wrong, as it lacks the “gradual” nuance.
Putting a command/volition in the second clause (×増えるにつれて買いなさい) → unnatural.
Getting the relationship wrong: につれて does not express a direct cause like ので/から.

rows: Along with A, B also changes
<ruby>年齢<rt>ねんれい</rt></ruby>につれて<ruby>視力<rt>しりょく</rt></ruby>が<ruby>落<rt>お</rt></ruby>ちる。
More formal; also carries the nuance of “according to/following”
<ruby>温度<rt>おんど</rt></ruby>の<ruby>上昇<rt>じょうしょう</rt></ruby>にしたがって<ruby>溶<rt>と</rt></ruby>ける。

Has both the meaning of simultaneity and of changing together
<ruby>成長<rt>せいちょう</rt></ruby>とともに<ruby>責任<rt>せきにん</rt></ruby>も<ruby>増<rt>ま</rt></ruby>す。

examples: Tokyo is an exciting, attractive city for young people.
A million yen is a lot of money to me, but to him it doesn't seem to be much.
To me, Japan is the country where I can make my dreams come true.
Deregulation is a pressing issue for both the government and private companies.
For me, home can only be that town where I spent my youth.
For international students, scholarships are a great support.
fields.explain:
Used to set a frame of evaluation; the predicate that follows is a property/evaluation.
Add は for emphasis/contrast; add も to extend the inclusion.
Do not use “Nにとって + action V” in the sense of “N does …”; use が/は instead.

• States a viewpoint/advantages and disadvantages/value from the standpoint of N: “for N, …”.
• Usually used with subjective judgments, but can also be an objective evaluation (when the target is a group/organization).
• Not used to indicate the agent performing an action.
fields.notes:
1) Easily confused with ～には.
→ ～にとって means “for (from N's standpoint)” and is used to evaluate/comment from N's point of view.
2) This pattern is usually followed by a judgment.
→ Example: 大切だ, 難しい, 便利だ… (evaluation).
3) Not used to indicate the direct target of an action.
→ If it means “doing something toward someone” (an action directed at them), consider ～に対して.
mistakes: Using “にとって” to indicate the agent performing an action (wrong function).
Using a direct action predicate (unnatural): use an adjective/judgment instead.
Confusing it with “に対して/について”: they differ in semantic purpose.
Forgetting “の” when modifying a noun: “NにとってのN2”.

rows: <ruby>私<rt>わたし</rt></ruby>にとって<ruby>大切<rt>たいせつ</rt></ruby>だ。
<ruby>専門<rt>せんもん</rt></ruby><ruby>家<rt>か</rt></ruby>からすると<ruby>危険<rt>きけん</rt></ruby>だ。
<ruby>子<rt>こ</rt></ruby>どもに<ruby>対<rt>たい</rt></ruby>して<ruby>優<rt>やさ</rt></ruby>しい。
Sets the subject matter, not a viewpoint of advantages and disadvantages
<ruby>政策<rt>せいさく</rt></ruby>について<ruby>議論<rt>ぎろん</rt></ruby>する。

examples: The meeting was held over three days.
The effects of the typhoon spread throughout the entire Kanto region.
He presented the results of twenty years of research.
The discussion went on until late at night.
They are active in a wide variety of fields.
My father has been doing this research for 20 years.
fields.explain:
The preceding N must be a unit of “coverage”: time (時間/日/年), space (地域/全域), quantity (回/項目), field (分野).
Formal nuance; used in narration and in describing scale/length.
Not used for very short/trivial spans; for short ones use ずっと/ずいぶん/長い間.

Expresses extending/spanning “throughout/all over” a period of time, scope, quantity or field. It focuses on breadth and duration; it does not necessarily mean nonstop continuity, but the degree of coverage is large.
• Usually used for considerable spans (several days, many years, nationwide...).
• Formal style, common in reports and news.
fields.notes:
• The modifier form “多岐にわたる + N” is a very common phrase in academic/PR writing.
• “長期にわたって/長時間にわたって” are set phrases often seen in the news.
• Does not combine directly with verbs (no “V にわたって”); nominalization is needed: “検討にわたって” is unnatural → “長期にわたる検討”. | Variants: ～にわたり・にわたる+N
mistakes: Using it with an N that does not indicate coverage: “気持ちにわたって” is wrong; use it with a specific time/scope.
Confusing it with “を通じて”: exams test the difference between “coverage” (にわたって) and “continuously throughout a period” (を通じて).
Forgetting the noun-modifying variant: choose “にわたるN” before a noun.

rows: <ruby>全国<rt>ぜんこく</rt></ruby>にわたって<ruby>影響<rt>えいきょう</rt></ruby>。
<ruby>一年<rt>いちねん</rt></ruby>を<ruby>通<rt>つう</rt></ruby>じて<ruby>暖<rt>あたた</rt></ruby>かい。

<ruby>明日<rt>あした</rt></ruby>にかけて<ruby>雨<rt>あめ</rt></ruby>。
<ruby>滞在<rt>たいざい</rt></ruby>の<ruby>間<rt>ま</rt></ruby>、<ruby>勉強<rt>べんきょう</rt></ruby>した。

examples: Contrary to expectations, the match ended in a lopsided score.
You must not go against the rules by eating or drinking in the classroom.
The proposal goes against the boss's wishes, but there are good grounds for it.
Unfortunately, the result turned out contrary to expectations.
Contrary to the weather forecast, it didn't rain.
Contrary to predictions
fields.explain:
Neutral to formal; can be used in both spoken and written language.
Emphasizes contrast with a norm/general expectation.
In the sense of “violation”, it carries a clear nuance of criticism/norms.

Expresses actions/results that are “contrary to, go against” rules, policies, expectations, forecasts... It can refer both to intentional actions (violations) and to objective results contrary to expectation.
• With normative nouns (規則/法律/方針), the meaning is close to “violate/oppose”.
• With nouns of expectation/prediction (期待/予想), it means “contrary to”.
fields.notes:
• “反する” is a Sino-Japanese verb with a formal nuance; its conjugations are “に反するN/に反したN/に反してV”.
• To say contrary to “what actually happened”, use ～のに/～にもかかわらず; “に反して” does not follow a verb clause but goes with nouns.
• Antonym pair: “～に沿って/～に即して” (following/in line with) vs “～に反して”.
explain: Expresses a result that is contrary to predictions, expectations or rules.
examples: 1. Aチームが勝つだろうという予想に反してBチームが勝った。
Contrary to predictions that Team A would win, Team B won.
2. 応募者数は当初の見込みに反し、非常に多かった。
Contrary to initial estimates, the number of applicants was very large.
3. 無断外泊は寮の規則に反する。
Staying out overnight without permission is against the dormitory rules.
4. 自由な言論を許さないのは憲法の精神に反する。
Not allowing free speech goes against the spirit of the constitution.
5. たとえ親の命令でも、自分の意思に反することはしたくない。
Even if my parents order me to, I don't want to do anything against my own will.
6. 予測／予報／教え／法律／意／期待／希望／願い　＋　に反して
Contrary to prediction / forecast / teachings / law / intention / expectation / hope / wish. explain: Expresses something contrary to, or in contrast with, a desire or expectation. N is usually a word such as: 予想、期待、命令、意図など ⏐ examples: 1. 専門家の予想に反して、景気は回復し始めた。
Contrary to the experts' predictions, the economy began to recover.
2. 我々の期待に反して、新商品はあまり売れなかった。
Contrary to our expectations, the new product did not sell very well.
mistakes: Using it after a verb clause: “来るに反して” is wrong; a noun is needed: “予想に反して来た”.
Confusing it with “に対して”: exams test “opposition to a norm” (に反して) vs “comparison/contrast” (に対して).
Forgetting the noun-modifying variant: choose the correct “に反するN/に反したN” before a noun.

examples: Please speak more gently to children.
Many objections were raised against his remarks.
We strengthened the support system for new employees.
My older brother is active, whereas my younger brother likes reading.
We'll hand out three to each person.
Sales rose 10% compared with the same period last year.
fields.explain:
Used with a noun referring to a person/organization/specific target when applying a policy, attitude or action.
Used for contrast when the two clauses are clearly parallel; for a simple comparison of degree, ～より/～に比べて is more natural.
In formal written language it can be shortened to に対し; to modify a noun, use に対するN.
Rarely used for a pure topic of discussion; for “about/regarding”, について/に関して is more natural.

• Target: expresses a behavior/attitude/measure directed toward a person/group/thing.
• Evaluation/praise and criticism: used when giving a comment aimed at a specific target (会社に対して厳しい意見, 親に対して失礼だ).
• Contrast: connects two clauses to emphasize a clear difference between A and B. Close in meaning to “while/on the other hand”.
• Ratio/per: states ratios or distribution (１人に対して２個, 男性１人に対して女性２人).
• Nuance: formal and more objective than について; not used for simple casual emotions.
fields.notes:
• に対して often goes with verbs of evaluation/attitude such as 優しい, 厳しい, 失礼だ, 敬意を払う, 批判する.
• The ratio structure “N1に対してN2” appears often in figures/statistics and reports.
• For contrast, you can write Aは…。それに対して、Bは… to separate the sentences clearly.
meaning_vi: A is…, while B is… (contrast/comparison)
explain: Used to set A and B against each other to highlight the difference: “A is…, while B is…”. Often appears in the form Aのに対してB.
examples: 1. あの二人はふたごなのに、兄はおとなしいのに対して、弟はよくしゃべる。
Although those two are twins, the older one is quiet, while the younger one talks a lot.
2. 近所のスーパーは夜１１時閉店なのに対し、コンビニは２４時間営業だ。
The nearby supermarket closes at 11 p.m., while the convenience store is open 24 hours.
3. この映画は海外では人気があるのに対して、日本国内ではそうでもない。
This movie is popular overseas, whereas in Japan it is not so popular.
4. 一般に、日本の若者は洋食を好む。それに対して、中高年は和食を好む。
In general, young Japanese people prefer Western food. In contrast, middle-aged and older people prefer Japanese food.
──────
1. 目上の人に対しては敬語を使わなければならない。
You must use keigo with your superiors.
2. 先生は学生のどんな質問に対しても、ていねいに答えてくれる。
The teacher answers any question from the students carefully.
3. 厳しい父に対し、私はいつも反抗的な態度をとった。
I always took a rebellious attitude toward my strict father.
4. 長引く不況で、国民の政府に対する不満が高まっている。
Because of the prolonged recession, people's dissatisfaction with the government is growing.
5. 彼女は自分に対して非常に厳しい人だ。
She is very strict with herself. meaning_vi: Toward, toward… (as for…), even toward…, …toward…. ⏐ explain: Used to express an attitude or action toward a matter or issue
Or used when presenting two contrasting things or matters ⏐ examples: 1. 田中先生は、生徒に対して厳しい。
Mr. Tanaka is strict with his students
2. まじめな長男に対して、次男は遊んでばかりで学校もよく休む。
In contrast to the diligent eldest son, the second son does nothing but play and often misses school explain: Used to indicate the target: toward some matter… The second clause usually contains words expressing an opposing relationship (words of resistance, opposition, refutation…) ⏐ examples: 1. 目上の人に対して、そういう言い方は失礼ですよ。
Speaking like that to a superior is rude.
2. 都市で人口が増えているのに対し、農村では減っている。
While the population is increasing in cities, it is decreasing in rural areas. | Modifier form: ～に対する + N
mistakes: Mixing it up with について/に関して: when just saying “about a topic”, prefer について; に対して can sound too stiff/formal.
Using に対して for a comparison of degree: for comparison, use ～より/～に比べて.
Forgetting to change to に対する when modifying a noun: ×学生に対して支援制度 → ○学生に対する支援制度.
Wrong order in the contrast structure: it must be “Aに対して、B…”.

examples: Compared with last year, there has been less rain this year.
Compared with the city, rent is cheaper in the countryside.
Compared with him, I'm short.
Compared with the previous film, this one has a faster pace.
Compared with speaking, I'm better at writing.
Compared with other countries, Japan is safe.
fields.explain:
Points out a specific standard in order to show a gap in degree. Suitable for commentary and analysis.
Usable in both spoken and written language; the form に比べ is concise written language.
Avoid comparing incompatible categories; items should be of the same category to sound natural.

• Expresses a comparison of degree against a clear reference point (Aに比べてBは…: B differs in degree from A).
• Emphasizes the criterion/aspect of comparison; often used with ほう, より, ほど to clarify the degree.
• Often used with figures, points in time, places, products, or people/things of the same kind, to avoid mismatched comparisons.
fields.notes:
• Often used with figures: 去年に比べて10％増, 昨日より2度高い.
• When B is clearly the subject, “Aに比べて、Bのほうが…” is often used.
• To compare clauses, use の for nominalization: 勉強するのに比べて…
explain: ◎ Expresses the meaning "Compared with ~, ~ is more".
examples: 1. 私の国に比べて、日本は人が多い。
Compared with my country, Japan has more people.
2. 前回に比べて、参加者が少ない。
Compared with last time, there are fewer participants.
meaning_vi: Expresses comparison. Compared with ~
explain: Used to compare A with B. ～に比べて is usually followed by a characteristic, an evaluation or figures that show the difference.
examples: 1. 昼間に比べて深夜は電器料金が安い。
Compared with the daytime, electricity is cheaper late at night.
2. 今年は例年に比べ、寒さが厳しいそうだ。
I hear the cold is more severe this year compared with an average year.
3. 女性のほうが男性に比べ平均寿命の長い国が多い。
In many countries, women have a longer average life expectancy than men.
4. 「私は話すのに比べて、書く力が弱いんです。」
Compared with speaking, my writing is weak.
──────
1. ①　去年に比べて
Compared with last year
2. ②　去年に比べて、今年は雪が多い。
Compared with last year, there is more snow this year.
3. ➂     とり肉は豚肉に比べ、脂が少ない。
Chicken has less fat than pork. meaning_vi: Compared with, in comparison with ⏐ explain: Used when comparing two things or matters ⏐ examples: 1. 試験問題は昨年に比べて易しくなった。
The exam questions became easier compared with last year
2. 店で買うのに比べ、通信販売は便利だが、欠点もある。
Compared with buying in a store, mail order is convenient, but it also has drawbacks
mistakes: Confusing it with に対して: ×Aに対してBのほうが高い → ○Aに比べてBのほうが高い.
Leaving out the subject being compared makes it ambiguous: include Bのほうが to make clear which side is greater.
Mismatched comparisons (of different kinds) are unnatural.
Wrong order: it must be “Aに比べて、B…”; do not invert the idea and leave out the subject.

fields.meaning:
Expresses the speaker's strong conviction.
［ふつう］　+　に違いない
［Na：ひまだN：雨だ］
fields.connection: V plain form + に違いない / N / Na / Aい
examples: It's already dark, but the lights aren't on. They must be out.
The culprit must be A. After all, A has a strong motive and no alibi.
If even Yamada, who has good grades, could only answer half of it, that exam must have been really difficult.
「Mr. Suzuki still isn't here, is he? He's not the type to be late, so something must have happened.」
It must be fully booked.
My umbrella is gone. Someone must have taken it.
fields.explain: Strongly asserts the speaker's conjecture based on evidence: “it must be…”. The speaker believes it is almost certainly true.
fields.notes:
1) Easily confused with ～はずだ／～に決まっている.
→ ～に違いない means “certainly” based on inference with evidence, but it is still the speaker's conjecture.
2) Not used for weak conjecture.
→ If you mean only “maybe”, use ～かもしれない／～だろう.
3) Often goes with signs/evidence.
→ There is usually prior information serving as the basis for the conclusion.
